newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand floats baht - details summary.
newsitem.headline: Thailand floats baht - details summary.

text.p: Here are details on the managed float of the baht announced by Thai financial authorities on Wednesday.
- The value of the baht would be set by market forces but the flotation would be managed by the authorities.
- The baht's peg against a basket of currencies would be discontinued.
Since 1984, the baht's midrate against the dollar has been fixed on a daily basis by the central bank based on a trade-weighted basket of currencies denominated by the dollar.
- The Bank of Thailand said it was raising its key bank rate to 12.5 percent from 10.5 percent, effective immediately.
The bank rate is the rate the central bank charges on loans to commercial banks.
- The Bank of Thailand said a baht-dollar reference rate would be set daily at the close of trade following the baht flotation.
The reference rate would be based on the baht's trading average the day before.
- The Bank of Thailand said it had an "appropriate rate" in mind to which it expected the baht to move.
If the rate went beyond the appropriate level the central bank said it would intervene in the market.
- Central bank officials said that under the new baht system they would be following the Singapore model of managing the currency, without elaborating.

- Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond said Thailand had sought technical assistance from the International Monetary Fund and the Reserve Bank of Australia. The RBA has since agreed to provide technical advice to the Bank of Thailand in the managed float.

- A two-tier baht market - one offshore and another onshore - that has been in place since the last speculative attack on the baht in May when the central bank imposed currency controls would remain for now but its future would be reviewed.
- The Bank of Thailand said it expected the baht to remain volatile in the short term after the flotation, but said the public need not panic.
_ The Bank of Thailand said it would intervene in foreign exchange markets from time to time to achieve its baht flotation policy objectives and guard against excessive fluctuation.
- Thai financial authorities will give businesses affected by the baht's flotation and volatile soft loans help to allow them to meet foreign debt repayments. No details given yet.
- The Bank of Thailand said foreigners and non-resident bank clients were banned from buying dollars for speculative purposes following the flotation.

- Foreigners failing to produce evidence of underlying business or investment transactions would not be allowed to buy dollars or raise dollar funds by selling short-term, baht-denominated money market instruments with less than six-month maturity.
- The Bank of Thailand said the restrictive measures were temporary.
